(a) "actual map of a nonempty finite union of parameter circles to the oriented (x,z) plane" (src 1826-1827). SmoothLoop (l.166): γ : ℝ → Plane, ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ, Function.Periodic γ 1; SmoothFront (l.305) c : ℕ, hc : 0 < c, comp : Fin c → SmoothLoop; bundle `map` (l.1542). A 1-periodic map of ℝ is exactly a map of the oriented circle ℝ/ℤ (orientation = increasing t); the plane orientation enters only through det (positive = counterclockwise, the def:positive-lift convention, src 328-331), used in transverse/crossSign/cusp_semicubical. The printed sentence does not name a regularity class; C^∞ is the standard "smooth" and the recorded reading FR-3 (AUTHOR_NOTES 3311ff). Faithful; C^∞ noted under stronger_than_source as a reading.

(b) "finitely many transverse double points" (src 1827-1828). doubles_finite (l.328) = finiteness of ordered pairs of distinct parameters in [0,1) with equal image; with no_triple each double point contributes exactly two ordered pairs, so this is finiteness of the double points. transverse (l.332): for all ¬SameParam p q with equal image, det(vel p, vel q) ≠ 0 — exactly linear independence of the two velocities. Bundle double_points (l.1547) restates both. Faithful. (transverse also forces cusp_alone since vel = 0 kills det; harmless overlap.)

(c) "ordinary semicubical cusps" (src 1828). IsCusp p := vel p = 0 (l.426); cusp_semicubical (l.318): deriv γ t = 0 → det(γ'' t, γ''' t) ≠ 0; cusps_finite (l.314). The standard (Whitney/Bruce–Giblin) characterisation of an A_2 = (u²,u³) cusp is γ' = 0 with γ'', γ''' independent; I checked it is reparametrization-invariant: at a zero of γ', (γ∘φ)'' = φ'²γ'', (γ∘φ)''' = φ'³γ''' + 3φ'φ''γ'', so det scales by φ'^5. On the printed germ (src 3217-3219 / sm-3:2747) det = 8A² (module l.933-941, statement only). Finiteness of cusps is automatic for this class, so cusps_finite adds no strength. Bundle `cusps` (l.1553). Faithful (FR-2).

(d) "no other singularities" (src 1828). Non-immersive points: every zero of γ' is subject to cusp_semicubical, so all singular parameters are ordinary cusps (bundle no_other_singularities first conjunct, l.1558, is Iff.rfl). Multiple points: only pairwise transverse double points (transverse), no triple points (no_triple l.335), none at a cusp (cusp_alone / transverse). Faithful.

(e) "no vertical tangencies on regular arcs" (src 1829). no_vertical (l.325): deriv ≠ 0 → (deriv).1 ≠ 0, i.e. x' ≠ 0 wherever γ' ≠ 0. Exact.

(f) "limiting tangent at every cusp nonvertical: ... x''(0) ≠ 0" (src 1829-1831). cusp_nonvertical (l.322): deriv = 0 → (iteratedDeriv 2 γ t).1 ≠ 0. At an ordinary cusp γ'' ≠ 0 spans the limiting tangent line (γ(t)-γ(0) = ½γ''t² + O(t³)), and under any regular reparametrization (γ∘φ)''(0) = φ'(0)²γ''(0), so x'' ≠ 0 is parametrization-invariant; the printed "semicubical parameter u" is therefore not needed. On the germ x'' = 2A. Faithful.

(g) "Cusps meet no other strand or singularity" (src 1831). cusp_alone (l.338): ¬SameParam p q → vel p = 0 → eval p ≠ eval q: the cusp point has no other preimage, which excludes another strand, another cusp and a double point at the cusp. Exact.

(h) "At a crossing the branch with smaller dz/dx is over" (src 1832). slope p = (vel p).2/(vel p).1 (l.516); IsOverUnder p q := IsDouble p q ∧ slope p < slope q (l.526). At a double point both branches are regular (cusp_alone) hence nonvertical (no_vertical) and transversal ⇒ slopes are finite and distinct, so exactly one branch is over (isOverUnder_xor, bundle over_rule l.1572). Exact.

(i) "A downward cusp is traversed from its locally upper arm to its locally lower arm" (src 1832-1833). IsDownCusp p := IsCusp p ∧ x''·det(γ'',γ''') < 0 (l.446, 457). Independent check: with a = γ''(0), b = γ'''(0), a₁ ≠ 0, the two arms at ±s have, at equal x, z(later) − z(earlier) = (s³/(3a₁))·det(a,b) + O(s⁴), so the later arm is the upper one iff a₁·det(a,b) > 0 and the traversal is upper→lower iff x''·det < 0; the same sign comes from the side of the nonvertical tangent line (det(a, p(t))·a₁ has sign of t·a₁·det(a,b)). Confirmed on the printed germ (16A³; germFront_later_arm_higher_iff l.945-960, statement). The rendering is a correct derivative-form definition of the printed notion (FR-2); the geometric equivalence is verified by hand, not in Lean, which is acceptable for a definition row. Bundle downward_cusp (l.1579) adds the complementary IsUpCusp and the Xor — harmless unpacking.

(j) D(F), w(F), s(F) (src 1833-1836). cuspSet (l.646) = one parameter per cusp (fundamental period; cusps are simple points by cusp_alone), downCount (l.724). crossingPairs (l.681) = doubleSet filtered by slope q.1 < slope q.2: each double point exactly once, in over-first order (crossingPairs_xor_swap). crossSign p q = if 0 < det(vel p, vel q) then 1 else -1 (l.529) = sgn det(u_over, u_under) since det ≠ 0 at double points (crossSign_eq_sign, bundle w_sum l.1597). writhe (l.728) = Σ over crossingPairs. sCount (l.730) = #crossingPairs + #cuspSet. All exact.

(k) rounding (src 1838-1841). GeomRounding F G (l.1129-1168), G : Fin F.c → SmoothLoop. "disjoint clean cusp discs": disc (IsDisc = compact convex nonempty interior, the accepted clean-disc vocabulary of LinkMoves.lean l.100), center (cusp point ∈ interior U c), disjoint; clean (l.1149) + arc_in (l.1152) give F⁻¹(U c) = [a c, b c] + ℤ on circle c and nothing from other circles; arc_simple (l.1154) makes F([a c,b c]) an embedded arc with no double point; len (b−a < 1) is the "no component entirely inside" clause; the frontier of U c is met only at F(a c), F(b c) (derivable: parameters just outside [a,b] map outside U). This is exactly "F ∩ U c is the single arc through the cusp", the meaning of "clean cusp disc", and matches the accepted `Clean` (frontier_injOn, exits) in content. "replace each cusp by a simple regular arc": agree (l.1157: G = F off the open arcs), inside, regular (deriv ≠ 0 on (a,b)), simple (InjOn); G is a C^∞ 1-periodic loop so it joins F to infinite order at a c, b c. "same oriented attachments": literal — same parameter circles, same orientation, same endpoints, velocities agree at the endpoints (deriv_eq_of_notMem, statement). "no crossing": no_crossing (l.1167): no point of a new arc is hit by any other parameter (other arcs, unchanged parts, itself). Not provably empty. "The resulting ordinary diagram is denoted S(F)": Rounding S = ⟨G, geom, marking : F.Marking S⟩ (l.1470), IsRounding S = Nonempty (l.1479), bundle resulting_diagram (l.1655). Bundle named_record (l.1661) restates it. (iii) rounding_no_crossing (l.1639) = the no_crossing field plus the consequence isDouble_iff ("creates no crossing"); rounding_ordinary (l.1647) = regular_everywhere, transverse, no_triple of G = "ordinary diagram" in the def:positive-lift sense (closed regular curves, transverse double points, no triple points; over choices via the Marking); no nonverticality is claimed for G, correctly, since the replacing arc must have a vertical tangent.
